summary: Gilbert's Cove Lighthouse, first lit 18 August 1904 on St. Mary's Bay, Digby County: a keeper's house with a lantern, kept by one family until 1972, now a museum.

structures.note: Painted white with red roofs in 1904
Height 11 m (36 ft) from base to top of ventilator, per 1904 report

access.note: Grounds, shore and picnic area free; tearoom, gift shop and museum inside the lighthouse. Gravel road 1.2 km from Route 1.

facts.agency: Gilbert Cove and District Historical Society (leases the property from the province)

events.note: Square wooden dwelling with lantern; contract to John Roney of Granville Ferry for $1,193
J. William (Willie Jane) Melanson, first keeper; Marine tables print 18 Aug 1904 (1915 table) and 18 Aug 1894 (1909 and 1910 tables)
Louise Melanson becomes official keeper when her father reaches 75 (LF: 1950; NSLPS keeper list: 1951)
Lighthouse Friends date. NSLPS gives automation by 1975 and before 1973; Rowlett inactive since 1975
Louise Melanson dies; the Melanson family's keeping of the light ends
Lantern light discontinued and replaced by an automated beacon on a concrete base (LF; Rowlett)
Gilbert Cove and District Historical Society formed; province leases the property to it
Repaired and opened as a small museum, tearoom and gift shop
Officially decommissioned (register); NSLPS dates the beacon's end to May 1984
Provincially Registered Property, recognized 17 June 1991 (register). LF and NSLPS give 1990
Repairs to tower and armour stone added against erosion; grants from NSLPS J. M. Kaplan Fund, government and ACOA

keepers.name: William Joseph Melanson
keepers.note: Known as 'Willie Jane'. Lighthouse Friends spells Joseph William. Marine tables print J. W. or Jos. W. Melanson at $300 a year. Appointment date printed 18 Aug 1904 (report year ended 31 Mar 1915) and 18 Aug 1894 (reports year ended 31 Mar 1909 and 1910): unresolved.

keepers.name: Louise Melanson
keepers.note: Daughter; official keeper. NSLPS keeper list gives 1951 to 1972; Lighthouse Friends gives 1950 to 1965 but its text has her in the light until her death in 1972.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Rowlett and Lighthouse Friends date the end of the lantern light to 1975. The NSLPS dates its beacon's end to May 1984, and the register says the lighthouse was officially decommissioned in 1984. The story gives both.
Lighthouse Friends says automation came in 1965; the NSLPS says by 1975 and before 1973; Rowlett says inactive since 1975. The story gives all three.
The register gives 17 June 1991 as the recognition date. Lighthouse Friends and the NSLPS give 1990. The record's 1991 follows the register.
NSLPS keeper list gives 1951 to 1972; Lighthouse Friends gives 1950 to 1965 but says she lived in the light until 1972. The roster uses 1950 to 1972 and names both.

notes_for_editor: Page images checked 2026-10-27 in the Internet Archive viewer, at the scan pages the footnotes give. In the 1915 table (printed p. 69, scan p. 76) the Nova Scotia row reads Gilbert point, J. W. Melanson, Aug. 18, 1904, 300 00. In the 1909 table (printed p. 160, scan p. 167) and the 1910 table (printed p. 255, scan p. 257) the row reads Gilbert Point, Jos. W. Melanson, Aug. 18, 1894, 300 00. Each name sits on the same row as its station, so the match is by row, not by column position. The conflict in appointment dates (1904 against 1894) is real and stays unresolved in the story. Lighthouse Friends' text and keeper line disagree about Louise Melanson's dates (1965 vs 1972). The 1904 report gives the range as 'seven miles', with no unit; the story keeps the report's word. The lens order disagrees: the 1904 report says seventh-order dioptric; Rowlett says sixth-order Fresnel. The height disagrees too: 36 ft in the 1904 report and NSLPS, 38 ft in Rowlett. The register text is read through Heritage Guide's word-for-word copy because historicplaces.ca did not render. The Digby Weekly Courier is read only as quoted by the NSLPS. No wreck, storm or rescue at the light was found in the sources read, so the chapter 'Storms, wrecks and rescues' is omitted. The Heritage Guide register also says the light is one of 'only two known lighthouses of this style to remain', while the NSLPS says one of 'only three of this type left in Nova Scotia'. Wikipedia was consulted for leads only and is not cited. Hours: Digby says open mid-June to late September; Rowlett says mid-June to mid-September.
